results.content: To address this issue, we previously proposed the Distributional Soft Actor-Critic (DSAC or DSACv1), an off-policy RL algorithm that enhances value estimation accuracy by learning a continuous Gaussian value distribution. In this paper, we introduce three key refinements to DSACv1 to overcome these limitations and further improve Q-value estimation accuracy: expected value substitution, twin value distribution learning, and variance-based critic gradient adjustment. [11] proposed clipped double Q-learning, an actor-critic-based approach that incorporates the minimum value between two Q-estimates in formulating the learning arXiv:2310.05858v7 [cs.LG] 6 Aug 2025 Please refer to the journal version: IEEE TPAMI 2025 DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2025.3537087 objective for both Q-value and policy functions. In [18], we have introduced a standard version of the distribu-tional soft actor-critic algorithm (also termed DSACv1) to enhance value estimation accuracy by learning a Gaussian distribution of random returns, referred to as the value distribution, rather than focusing solely on the expected return (i.e., Q-value). This algorithm incorporates three key refinements to standard DSAC, in-cluding expected value substituting, twin value distribution learning, and variance-based critic gradient adjustment.
